# SimpleLayout — stack children along an axis

The stacking idiom: siblings placed one after another along
`axis`, in child order, `spacing` apart (negative overlaps). The cross axis
and all sizes stay the children's own — a child centers itself across a row
with the ordinary `y = center`. Invisible children are skipped and their
space reclaimed; a skipped child still gets the slot it would occupy, so
re-showing it needs no special case. A `Spacer` child flexes to absorb the
run's slack along the axis (between two groups it pushes them apart; one on
each side centers the run).

Written in Declare over the Layout kernel: the whole strategy is this one
pure place() — one box per laid child, aligned by index.

```declare
col: View [ x = 20, y = 20,
    layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 8 ],
    View [ width = 160, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = steelblue ],
    View [ width = 120, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = cadetblue ],
    View [ width = 190, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6, fill = slategray ]
    ]
```

## axis
Which way children stack: `y` (the default) or `x`. **A bare literal, not a string** —
`axis = x`, and note that `x` here is the axis token, not the position attribute.

## spacing
The gap between adjacent children. **Negative overlaps them**, which is how a stack of
cards or avatars is built.

## place()
The whole strategy: one box per laid child, positioned along the axis in child order.
**The cross axis and every size stay the children's own** — a child centres itself
across a row with the ordinary `y = center`. Override it in a subclass for custom
geometry; a `Layout`'s `place()` **may** aggregate over children, which is the one place
that is allowed.
*/

class SimpleLayout extends Layout [
    axis: Axis = y,
    spacing: number = 0,

    place() {
        const axis = this.axis
        const size = axis == "x" ? "width" : "height"
        const kids = this.laid()
        const flexing = (c) => (c).flexes === true

        // slack, only when someone flexes: the view's extent along the axis
        // minus the rigid content and the gaps between visible children
        // a child's slot is its FOOTPRINT (the scale/rotation-composed box),
        // so a scale = 0.5 child occupies half the run and a rotated card
        // reserves what it visibly covers; the box's lead compensates the
        // transform's own offset so the VISIBLE edge lands on the slot
        let each = 0
        let flexN = 0
        for (const c of kids) if (c.visible && flexing(c)) flexN = flexN + 1
        if (flexN > 0) {
            let content = 0
            let visN = 0
            for (const c of kids) {
                if (!c.visible) continue
                visN = visN + 1
                if (!flexing(c)) content = content + (c).footprint()[size]
            }
            const extent = this.view == null ? 0 : (this.view)[size]
            each = Math.max(0, (extent - content - this.spacing * Math.max(0, visN - 1)) / flexN)
        }

        let pos = 0
        return kids.map((c) => {
            const flex = c.visible && flexing(c)
            // footprint, never bounds: the strategy must not read the slot it
            // writes (one-pass discipline). A flexing child's size is ALLOCATED
            // (box.w/h), so its footprint is never consulted — lead 0, raw slot.
            const f = flex ? null : (c).footprint()
            const lead = f == null ? 0 : (axis == "x" ? f.x : f.y)
            const box = (axis == "x" ? ({ x: pos - lead }) : ({ y: pos - lead }))
            if (flex) box[axis == "x" ? "w" : "h"] = each
            if (c.visible) pos = pos + (flex ? each : (f)[size]) + this.spacing
            return box
            })
        }
    ]

# AppIsland — a whole Declare program running inside a box

`AppIsland` embeds a live Declare application: give it a `program` and it mounts
that program as its own child app — its own reactive graph, input router, and
stage — sized to this view's box. There is no coordinate sync: the tenant fills
the box, so your width/height constraints size it like any view.

It composes `DOMIsland` (the sanctioned foreign-content leaf) and builds the
host's mount key from structured inputs, so callers never hand-splice the
`run:…` wire. The page host (`browser/host-client.js`) sees the key on the box,
resolves the program on its boot ladder — prewarm → cache → in-browser compile,
identical on the dev server and a static host — and renders the child.

`childName` (inherited from `DOMIsland`) is the reverse channel: the running child's
`appName` reflected back up, so a host can title itself by what it shows.

## The bridge

An AppIsland carries the ISLAND BRIDGE (guide ch. 18): declare `external`
attributes on the instance and they pair, by name and with a type handshake,
against the tenant program's own `external` declarations — typed facts both
ways, per settle. `post(topic, payload)` / `onPost(m: IslandPost)` carry the
verbs. `env` and `childName` below are the bridge's untyped ancestors and
still work; new code should declare its surface.

The window frame, activation, and titling belong to the caller — a desktop window
adds an `onPointerDown` that raises itself and reads `childName` for its title; the
homepage and the viewer just size the box. This primitive is only the embedding.

## program
What to run: a program name, a relative path (`"../../calendar/calendar"` reaches the
real app — **no copy of the source, ever**), or the reserved `"__raw__"` live-edit
channel, where the running program is the host app's `liveSource` and recompiles as it
changes. **`""` detaches the island** and nothing mounts, which is how a closed panel
stops paying for its tenant — and what bounds the recursion when a program embeds a
view of itself.

## env
The embedding environment in query form (`"dark=1&base=../x/"`), delivered to the
child's reactive `app.env` at mount **and on every change**. Empty sends none, so the
child keeps its own defaults — leave it alone unless the host genuinely overrides
something, or you will pin the child's appearance against the system's.
*/

class AppIsland extends DOMIsland [
    program: string = "",
    env: string = "",

    // the host mount key: `run:<program>`, with the env query after `|`. No
    // program → empty slot → the island stays detached (DOMIsland unmounts it).

    slot = { this.program == "" ? "" : "run:" + this.program + (this.env == "" ? "" : "|" + this.env) }
    ]

/*
# Control

The interaction-state base every stateful control extends (docs/system-design/components-baseline.md,
Contract 3). It owns how the pointer, keyboard, and focus relate to this view — and
nothing semantic: `checked`, `value`, and their kin live on the concrete control.

The pointer half is the language's now: `hovered` and `pressed` are View's read-only
interaction intrinsics (chain-based, touch-correct, cancel-safe). What Control adds is
the CONTROL policy on top of them, as derivations every concrete control reads:

- `hot` / `down` — the styling pair: the intrinsics gated by `disabled`, with the
  keyboard-activation `flash` folded into `down`. Style against these, not the raw
  intrinsics, and a disabled control never lights up.
- `disabled` — inert: not focusable, no activation; concrete controls gate on it.
- keyboard — Space or Enter on the focused control activates it, the same `press()`
  path a pointer uses, acknowledged by flashing the pressed look.

It also owns the two things every labelled control was improvising:

- `iconLeft` / `iconRight` — decoration, by class name. A concrete control lays
  them out; Control only declares that they exist, so `Button` and `Segment`
  answer to one vocabulary.
- `menu` — the ROLE of dropping a menu. Not decoration: fifteen sites across the
  corpus call `someMenu.openFor(control)`, and the disclosure mark for that one
  role was drawn five different ways or omitted (a glyph inside the label string
  in five places, a private chevron in two, a separate `Text` in one, nothing in
  `MenuBar` and `DataGrid`). Nobody chose those differences. Setting `menu` gets
  the mark, the anchored open, the held-open styling, and Down-to-open together,
  which is the part a hand-rolled copy gets wrong one piece at a time.

Extend it to make your own control a first-class one — focusable, keyboard-activated,
and styled off the same state pair as everything the library ships:

```declare
class Stepper extends Control [ width = 90, height = 26, cornerRadius = 6,
    n: number = 0,
    fill = { down ? theme.controlPressed : hot ? theme.controlHover : theme.control },
    press() { n = n + 1 },
    onClick() { if (!disabled) press() },
    t: Text [ x = center, y = center, fontSize = 13, text = { "" + classroot.n } ]
    ]


App [ Stepper [ x = 20, y = 20 ] ]
```

## disabled
Inert: not focusable, no activation, and the gate folded into `hot`/`down` so a
disabled control never lights up. **Constrain it rather than assigning it**
(`disabled = { app.muted }`) — it is ordinary derived state. Concrete controls also
dim themselves against `theme.disabledOpacity`.

## hot
Hover under control policy — `hovered` gated by `disabled`. **Style against this, not
the raw `hovered` intrinsic**, or a disabled control lights up under the pointer. Always
false on touch, since `hovered` is.

## down
The pressed look — the `pressed` intrinsic gated by `disabled`, **with keyboard
activation folded in**, so Space/Enter flashes the same appearance a pointer press
gives. The other half of the styling pair with `hot`.

## focused
True while this control holds keyboard focus. For the *ring*, you want nothing: the
app-level `FocusRing` indicates focus for you. Read this only for a control's own
focus styling.

## focusVisible
Focused **and** the focus arrived by keyboard — the web's `:focus-visible` channel.
Cleared by blur and by a pointer press on this control, so a clicked control shows no
keyboard edge while a tabbed one does. What a `Pane` header's focus edge reads.

## iconLeft
A decorative icon for the leading slot, **named by class** (`iconLeft = "TrashIcon"`),
not nested as a child — a control is a leaf, and a name is the one form where authored
and data-bound are the same mechanism (`iconLeft = { "" + :icon }` in a replicated
toolbar). Control only declares the slot; the concrete control lays it out. A
**computed** name needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build, since no static reference
reaches it.

## iconRight
The trailing icon slot, same vocabulary as `iconLeft`. Setting it **wins over the
chevron a `menu` would imply** — see `rightIcon`.

## menu
The menu this control drops — an instance, not a name (`menu = { app.optionsMenu }`).
Setting it is a *role*, not decoration: the disclosure mark, the anchored open below
the control, the held-open fill, and ArrowDown-to-open all follow together. **Declare
one menu and point many controls at it** rather than one per opener; the menu reads
`opener` to vary its items.

## menuOpen
True while `menu` is showing *and* this control is what opened it. **Derived, never
written** — a flag set on open goes stale the moment the menu closes some other way
(Escape, a pick, a press on the backdrop) and strands the control in its held-open
look forever.

## rightIcon
What actually renders on the right: `iconRight` when set, else the disclosure chevron
implied by `menu`, else nothing. One place decides, so every menu-dropping control in
the corpus wears the same mark.

## flash
The keyboard-activation pulse — the control's own state, since the `pressed` intrinsic
is the pointer's truth and is read-only. Folded into `down`, so styling needs to read
only the pair.

## flashMs
How long `flashPress()` holds the pressed look.

## openMenu()
Opens `menu` anchored to this control, unless there is none or the control is disabled.
The seam a concrete control calls from its own `press()`.

## press()
**The activation seam — override this, not the handlers.** Pointer and keyboard both
land here, so one override serves a click, Space, and Enter. The base opens `menu` when
there is one. A value control delivers through `input` from here and **never writes its
own value slot directly**, which is what lets a bound control avoid fighting its
constraint.

## focusShape()
The focus silhouette the ring hugs, `{ x, y, w, h, rad }` in this control's own
coordinates. `null` (the default) rings the whole bounds at its `cornerRadius`. Override
to ring the part that means something — a `Radio` rings its dot, a `Slider` its thumb.

## flashPress()
Flashes the pressed look to acknowledge keyboard activation — the platform convention
for buttons and menu items. **Value controls whose state change is itself the feedback
(Checkbox, Switch, Radio) deliberately do not call it.**

## onFocus
Records focus and captures the keyboard modality into `focusVisible`. An override must
keep both or the focus channel goes dark.

## onBlur
Clears `focused` and `focusVisible`.

## onPointerDown
Claims focus, clears the `:focus-visible` channel, and opens `menu` if there is one —
menus open on **press**, not release, as the platform does. **An override must keep the
`Focus.focus(this)` call**, or clicking the control strands the keyboard elsewhere.

## onKeyDown
Space and Enter run `press()`; ArrowDown opens `menu`. Ignores auto-repeat.
*/

class Control extends View [
    disabled: boolean = false,
    focused:  boolean = false,

    // A control is chrome, not prose: its label never selects, even inside a
    // `selectable` region (a provision here vetoes the inherited value — the
    // language rule: anything that activates declares itself unselectable).

    selectable = false,

    // the styling pair — the interaction intrinsics under CONTROL policy

    hot:  boolean = { this.hovered && !this.disabled },
    down: boolean = { (this.pressed && !this.disabled) || this.flash },

    // The :focus-visible channel for the control's OWN styling (a Tab header's
    // focus edge): focused AND the focus arrived by keyboard. Captured at the
    // focus event (the web's rule), cleared by blur — and by a pointer press on
    // this very control, the one case with no focus event (Focus.focus on the
    // already-focused target is a no-op, but the modality still cleared).

    focusVisible: boolean = false,

    focusable = { !this.disabled },

    // The keyboard affordance is the app-level FocusRing (focusring.declare —
    // one traveling indicator, declared once in the App), not a per-control
    // ring; `focused` stays declared here for controls' own styling.

    // ── content slots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    //
    // Icons by CLASS NAME, resolved through the tag registry. A name rather than
    // a child because a control is a leaf — everything else about it is an
    // attribute — and because an attribute is the one form where authored and
    // bound are the same mechanism: `iconLeft = TrashIcon` and
    // `iconLeft = { "" + :icon }` in a replicated toolbar are one slot.

    iconLeft:  string = "",
    iconRight: string = "",

    // The menu this control drops. Set it and the disclosure mark, the anchored
    // open, and the open-state styling all follow; `openMenu()` is the seam a
    // concrete control calls from its own `press()`.

    menu: View = null,

    // DERIVED, not written. A flag set on open goes stale the moment the menu
    // closes some other way — Escape, a pick, a click on the backdrop — and the
    // button keeps its held-open fill for the rest of the session. Reading the
    // menu's own state cannot drift: it is open if the menu is shown AND this
    // control is what opened it (one menu serves many openers).

    menuOpen: boolean = { this.menu != null
                       && (this.menu).shown === true
                       && (this.menu).opener === this },

    // What a control SHOWS on the right: an explicit icon wins, else the
    // disclosure chevron a `menu` implies. One place decides, so the five
    // improvised indicators become one.

    rightIcon: string = { this.iconRight != "" ? this.iconRight : this.menu != null ? "ChevronIcon" : "" },

    openMenu() {
        if (this.menu == null || this.disabled) return
        ;(this.menu).openFor(this)
        },

    // the activation seam — concrete controls override; pointer and keyboard both land here

    press() { if (this.menu != null) this.openMenu() },

    // the control's FOCUS SILHOUETTE — override to ring something other than
    // the whole bounds (a Radio rings its dot). null = bounds + cornerRadius.
    // { x, y, w, h, rad } in the control's own coordinates.

    focusShape() { return null },

    // keyboard activation's visual acknowledgment: flash the pressed look
    // (the platform convention for buttons — and menu items, later). Value
    // controls whose state change IS the feedback (Checkbox, Switch, Radio)
    // don't call this. `flashMs` is per-control tunable. `flash` is the
    // control's OWN state — the `pressed` intrinsic is the pointer's truth and
    // is read-only; a keyboard pulse is a different fact, folded into `down`.

    flash:   boolean = false,
    flashMs: number  = 220,

    flashPress() {
        this.flash = true
        setTimeout(() => { this.flash = false }, this.flashMs)
        },

    onFocus() { this.focused = true; this.focusVisible = Focus.byKeyboard() },
    onBlur()  { this.focused = false; this.focusVisible = false },

    // a click is also a focus claim — the keyboard picks up where the pointer left

    // A MENU opens here, not from `onClick`. Every other control routes the
    // pointer through `press()` (`onClick() { if (!disabled) press() }`), but
    // Button inverts that — its `onClick` is the USE SITE's action slot — so a
    // menu hung off `press()` opened from the keyboard and never from a click.
    // Pointer-down is also what the platform does: menus open on press, not
    // release. The keyboard keeps its own path through `press()`, and the two
    // cannot double-fire because a key press raises no pointer event.

    onPointerDown() {
        if (this.disabled) return
        this.focusVisible = false
        Focus.focus(this)
        if (this.menu != null) this.openMenu()
        },

    // Down opens a menu control — the platform convention, and the reason `menu`
    // is a role rather than an icon: an author who wired a chevron by hand never
    // got this.

    onKeyDown(e: KeyEvent) {
        if (this.disabled || e.repeat) return
        if (e.key == "Enter" || e.key == " ") this.press()
        else if (e.key == "ArrowDown" && this.menu != null) this.openMenu()
        }
    ]

/*
# Icon — the drawn mark

A small monochrome mark, **drawn** rather than typed. Fonts are not UI objects:
their glyphs are not guaranteed to be present, they rasterize differently on
every platform, and the ones that exist are the wrong shapes — a `✓` sits on the
text baseline and reads like a square-root sign, not like a checkmark. The house
already knew this in three places before it had a name for it (`Checkbox.mark`,
`Menu.check`, `Combobox.disc` are all drawn); this is that decision, stated once.

### Writing one

Subclass and override `draw`. Author the shape in a **16×16 box** — `unit`
converts it to whatever size the host asked for:

```declare-fragment
class SparkIcon extends Icon [
    draw(d: Draw) {
        d.scale(unit, unit)
        d.strokeStyle = ink; d.lineWidth = weight / unit
        d.beginPath(); d.moveTo(8, 1); d.lineTo(8, 15); d.stroke()
        }
    ]
```

Overriding a **method** is the refinement path that works — re-opening an
inherited child is not (`cap:` on a `Button` subclass fails at instantiate), so
the shape lives in `draw` and everything adjustable is a slot.

### Size changes the drawing, not the shape

Every icon is ONE path. There are no per-size variants, no thresholds, nothing
redrawn at a breakpoint: `unit` scales the 16-box to whatever the host asked for,
so a 64px icon is the 16px icon at 4×, exactly.

The **stroke** is the deliberate exception. `d.lineWidth = weight / unit` sits
*inside* `d.scale(unit, unit)`, so the two cancel and the line lands at a constant
`weight` in **device pixels at every size**. An icon's line therefore matches the
1px rules and text weights it sits among, instead of fattening as it grows.

The cost is that the stroke-to-size ratio falls: 1.6px is 10% of a 16px icon, 5%
at 32, 2.5% at 64. Across 14–18px, which is every site in this corpus, that is
invisible. Past ~32 an icon starts reading as a fine-line drawing rather than a
mark — so **this set is built for chrome sizes**, and a large display icon (an
empty-state mark, an about-box graphic) would want the opposite: `d.lineWidth =
weight` *outside* the scale, so the line grows with the drawing. Real icon
systems take a third road and redraw per optical size range; that is a bigger
undertaking than this set needs.

`test/probe/iconbook.declare` shows the ramp — the same chevron and bulb at 16,
24, 32, 48 and 64 — if the tradeoff ever needs re-judging.

### What is NOT an Icon

Application art. The desktop's dock icons are the case to look at before
reaching for this class: they rest at 56px and grow under the magnification
swell, they are polychrome (`gradient(hue1, hue2)` behind a hue-parameterised
drawing), and their **width animates every frame**. Each of those alone rules
them out — the constant stroke that suits a 16px mark is 2.9% of a 56px one and
reads spindly; `ink` is a single colour; and an animated width is the one thing
this set forbids.

The line is not "drawn versus not drawn" — dock art is drawn too. It is
**chrome vocabulary versus identity**. A mark that says *close*, *expand*,
*checked*, *this is the dark theme* belongs here, at a size the host states.
A mark that says *this is Calendar* does not, and belongs to the app that owns
the identity.

Desktop has both, which is what makes it the clarifying example: its menu rows
take `WindowIcon` and `CodeIcon` from this set, while its dock keeps `DockIcon`.

### Two rules

**Scale inside the body, never with the View's `scale`.** A recording rasterizes
into a canvas sized to its own ink bounds at device resolution
(`dom-backend.ts` `rasterize()`), while `scale` is a CSS transform applied
*after* — so `scale = { width / 16 }` would rasterize 16 pixels and stretch them.
Crisp at exactly 16, soft at every other size, which is most of them. Scaling
inside the recording allocates the raster at true size instead.

**Never animate an icon's `width`.** Reading size inside `draw` makes the
recording size-dependent: an animated size re-records AND reallocates the backing
canvas every frame, which is what dragged the dock's magnification from 60 to
~25fps (`adaptive-draw-cache.md`). A static size re-records once and costs
nothing after. Measured: 120 icons re-recording their *content* every frame runs
frame-bound at 16.6ms, cheaper than the 120 text glyphs they replace.

Colour is not a rule — `ink` follows the prevailing text colour, so an icon beside
a muted label goes muted on its own, and a host that needs a different ink (a
menu row's check inverting on the hot row) simply sets it.

## ink
The mark's colour. Follows the **prevailing `textColor`**, so an icon beside a muted
label goes muted on its own. **The trap: that slot falls back to black platform-wide**,
so an icon in a context that never states a text colour renders black and vanishes on a
dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets one — `IconHost` does it for
every icon built by name.

## weight
Stroke width in **final device pixels, not authored ones**. Divide by `unit` inside
`draw` (`d.lineWidth = weight / unit`) and the scale cancels, so the line lands at a
constant weight at every size and matches the 1px rules and text it sits among.

## unit
The 16-box-to-host-size scale factor. **Multiply the path by it; divide the stroke by
it.** Every icon is one path at one size, scaled — there are no per-size variants.

## isIcon
**Internal.** The marker a layout keys on to place an icon without knowing which shape
it is — not API.
*/

/*
# IconHost — a named icon, materialized

   A control names its icon (`iconLeft = TrashIcon`) rather than nesting one,
   because a control is a leaf and everything else about it is an attribute — and
   because an attribute is the one form where AUTHORED and BOUND are the same
   mechanism. `IconHost` is what turns that name into a live view, through the
   same `app.createView` seam the menu's `iconKind` already uses.

   It reserves no space when empty, so a control's `contentWidth` measures only
   the slots that are actually filled and an icon-less button needs no special
   case.

   LIMITATION, deliberate for now: the name is consumed once, at construction.
   A control whose icon must CHANGE at runtime (a play/pause toggle) is not
   served by this yet — that needs a name-valued slot the runtime re-materializes
   on change, which is a runtime feature, not a library one. Every site in this
   corpus names its icon statically.

## kind
The icon **class name** to build (`"TrashIcon"`). `""` builds nothing and the host
collapses to zero width, so an icon-less control needs no special case. **Consumed once,
at construction** — assigning a new name later does not re-materialize the icon. A name
that is only ever computed needs `use [ Name ]` to survive the build.

## ink
The colour handed to the icon this host builds. **`createView` cannot pass attributes,
so a prevailing slot is the only channel that reaches it** — this publishes `textColor`
for exactly that. Defaults to `theme.text` rather than the platform's inherited black,
which is what stops a host-built icon from rendering invisibly on a dark surface.

## onInit
Builds the named icon. Fires once.
*/

class IconHost extends View [
    kind: string = "",
    width  = { classroot.kind == "" ? 0 : this.iconSize },
    height = { this.iconSize },
    y = center,
    visible = { classroot.kind != "" },

    // THE INK CHANNEL. `createView` cannot pass attributes, so the only way to
    // reach the icon it builds is a PREVAILING slot — and the one `Icon.ink`
    // reads is `textColor`. Publishing it here is what lets a host state its
    // ink at all.
    //
    // The default matters more than it looks: prevailing `textColor` falls back
    // to 0x000000 platform-wide, so an icon that inherited it rendered BLACK —
    // fine on a light surface by luck, invisible on a dark one. Every
    // host-created icon in the corpus was doing that. `theme.text` is a floor
    // that is never invisible in either palette.

    ink: Color = { this.theme.text },
    textColor = { classroot.ink },

    onInit() { if (this.kind != "") this.createView(this.kind, ({ })) }
    ]


class Icon extends View [
    // The marker a layout keys on, so a control can place its icon without
    // caring which shape it is (the Segment/Segmented discipline).

    isIcon: boolean = true,

    // Size comes from the CONTEXT: `iconSize` is prevailing, so a menu states 16
    // once and every icon in every row answers. A use site may override it.

    width  = { this.iconSize },
    height = { this.width },
    y = center,

    // Follows the PREVAILING text colour, so an icon beside a muted label goes
    // muted on its own. The trap: that slot falls back to 0x000000 platform-wide,
    // so an icon in a context which never states a text colour renders BLACK and
    // disappears on a dark surface. State `ink` unless you know the context sets
    // one — `IconHost` does it for every icon built by name.

    ink: Color = { this.textColor },
    weight: number = 1.6,        // stroke width in FINAL pixels, not authored ones

    // 16-box → host size. Multiply the path by this; divide the stroke by it, so
    // the line keeps its true weight instead of scaling with the drawing.

    unit: number = { this.width / 16 }
    ]

/*
# Segmented

A row of mutually exclusive choices — the control you reach for when the options
are few, named, and worth showing all at once. Its choices are **data**, like
`Menu`'s items and `DataGrid`'s columns:

```declare-fragment
Segmented [ width = 300, value = { app.page },
    choices = { [ ({ id: "controls", label: "Controls" }),
                 ({ id: "table",    label: "Table" }),
                 ({ id: "grid",     label: "DataGrid" }) ] },
    input(v: object) { app.page = "" + v }
    ]
```

### Why data, and not `Segment` children

Because the sliding highlight cannot be built any other way. The pill has to know
which choice is selected and how wide each one is, and a constraint may not ask
the view tree that: `childViews` carries **set membership only**, so `.length` is
live while anything reaching into the collection is refused —
`aggregation over a reactive node collection … derive from data [DECLARE7001]`.
The compiler names the answer.

picks from a `ForEach`, Ant Design takes `options`; only Material and WinUI name
the item at all, and both compound it. A bare `Segment` class was the minority
pattern — and bare enough that two apps in this corpus had taken the name for a
paragraph of prose.

### Equal widths — a choice, not a limitation

Segments divide the control's width evenly. This is a DESIGN decision and it
could be otherwise: a `Layout`'s `place()` may aggregate over children — that is
how `SimpleLayout` sizes a variable-width row — so a strategy that placed each
segment by its own label and interpolated the pill between neighbours is
buildable. The `DECLARE7001` refusal binds constraints reaching into the view
tree, not the layout strategy whose job that is. Three reasons not to:

- **The systems that call this a segmented control agree.** The native ones
  divide evenly by default, as does the classic
  segmented `Picker`. The ones that size to content — Bootstrap, Ant — are really
  styling a row of buttons.
- **The segmented convention makes it a content rule**: keep segment labels short and
  similar in length. Equal width enforces that rather than tolerating it. One long
  label makes the whole control look wrong, which is the feedback you want.
- **The sliding pill.** At equal widths it translates at constant width. At
  variable widths it would have to morph its width WHILE travelling, which reads
  as rubbery and worsens the more the labels differ. Most platforms never meet
  this, because their highlight pops.

The cost is real and worth stating plainly: **a `Segmented` does not self-size to
its labels.** Set `width`, or accept `segMin × choices.length`.

The highlight springs a NORMALIZED LANE — a float index — not pixels. `x` is then
`lane × segW`, so a resize recomputes `segW` and the pill **snaps** to the right
place instead of skating across the bar on every layout change. Calendar's tab
strip discovered this; it is the one thing the bespoke copies did better than the
library, and it is now here.

The look is the library's: the chosen segment wears a raised `surface` pill with
a hairline. The motion is calendar's. Neither app was wrong about the half it got
right (`chrome-divergences.md` D9).

        d.strokeStyle = this.ink

        // self-loading: the ?segments payload carries the same metrics
        if (m == null && this.root.segSrc.value) {
            try { const p = JSON.parse(this.root.segSrc.value); m = (p && p.metrics) || null } catch (e) { m = null }
            }
        // a static host serves the raw file but answers no ?segments — count
        // the lines HERE, so the label holds on every hosting mode
        if (m == null && this.root.rawText() != "") m = this.localMetrics(this.root.rawText())
        return m == null ? "" : "· " + m.total + " lines, " + m.code + " code"
        },

    // the compiler's line classification in miniature: comments mask OUT,
    // """ text blocks and whole { } constraint bodies mask IN (a // inside a
    // body is body, not comment — the compiler's rule), and a line counts
    // as code when anything masked-in and non-blank survives on it

    localMetrics(src: string) -> object {
        const s = "" + src
        const n = s.length
        let total = 0
        let code = 0
        let has = false
        let depth = 0                            // { } body nesting — everything inside is code
        let inBlock = false                      // /* */ outside a body — comment
        let inText = false                       // """ block — code
        let bodyBlock = false                    // /* */ inside a body — still code, braces ignored
        let i = 0
        while (i < n) {
            const c = s[i]
            if (c == "\n") { total = total + 1; if (has) code = code + 1; has = false; i = i + 1; continue }
            if (inBlock) { if (c == "*" && s[i + 1] == "/") { inBlock = false; i = i + 2 } else i = i + 1; continue }
            if (inText) {
                if (c != " " && c != "\t" && c != "\r") has = true
                if (c == "\"" && s[i + 1] == "\"" && s[i + 2] == "\"") { inText = false; i = i + 3 } else i = i + 1
                continue
                }
            if (depth > 0) {
                if (c != " " && c != "\t" && c != "\r") has = true
                if (bodyBlock) { if (c == "*" && s[i + 1] == "/") { bodyBlock = false; i = i + 2 } else i = i + 1; continue }
                if (c == "/" && s[i + 1] == "*") { bodyBlock = true; i = i + 2; continue }
                if (c == "/" && s[i + 1] == "/") { while (i < n && s[i] != "\n") i = i + 1; continue }
                if (c == "\"" || c == "'") {
                    const q = c
                    i = i + 1
                    while (i < n && s[i] != q) { if (s[i] == "\\") i = i + 1; i = i + 1 }
                    i = i + 1
                    continue
                    }
                if (c == "{") depth = depth + 1
                if (c == "}") depth = depth - 1
                i = i + 1
                continue
                }
            if (c == "/" && s[i + 1] == "*") { inBlock = true; i = i + 2; continue }
            if (c == "/" && s[i + 1] == "/") { while (i < n && s[i] != "\n") i = i + 1; continue }
            if (c == "\"" && s[i + 1] == "\"" && s[i + 2] == "\"") { inText = true; has = true; i = i + 3; continue }
            if (c == "\"" || c == "'") {
                const q = c
                has = true
                i = i + 1
                while (i < n && s[i] != q) { if (s[i] == "\\") i = i + 1; i = i + 1 }
                i = i + 1
                continue
                }
            if (c == "{") { depth = 1; has = true; i = i + 1; continue }
            if (c != " " && c != "\t" && c != "\r") has = true
            i = i + 1
            }
        if (n > 0 && s[n - 1] != "\n") { total = total + 1; if (has) code = code + 1 }
        return ({ total: total, code: code })
        },
    dirName() { const p = this.root.filePath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? "" : p.slice(0, i + 1) },
    baseName() { const p = this.root.filePath(); const i = p.lastIndexOf("/"); return i < 0 ? p : p.slice(i + 1) },

    // the editor foreground (plain text / punctuation) behind the accent spans

    codeFg() { return this.root.isDark ? 0xABB2BF : 0x24292F },

    // role → color, theme-aware. Keys match the <span class> names highlight()
    // emits: k t a s n h p o b c. Dark = One Dark; light = a cool, light-native
    // set (gold-on-white reads as a dark-mode leftover, so types go purple/blue).

    codeAccents() {
        return this.root.isDark
            ? ({ k: 0xC678DD, t: 0xE5C07B, a: 0xE06C75, s: 0x98C379, n: 0xD19A66, h: 0x56B6C2, p: 0x61AFEF, o: 0x56B6C2, b: 0x9DA5B4, c: 0x6A737D })
            : ({ k: 0xCF222E, t: 0x8250DF, a: 0xB5452B, s: 0x1A7F37, n: 0x9A6700, h: 0x0E7490, p: 0x0550AE, o: 0xCF222E, b: 0x6B7280, c: 0x8A919C })
        },

    // What this app adds to the house palette, and nothing more.
    //
    // `codeBg` is the house BACKDROP showing through the page — a code well is
    // recessed, which is the same relationship in both modes and needs no value
    // of its own. `accentSecondary` is the far end of the brand gradient (the
    // wordmark, a card's spine, the live grip); the house has one accent, and a
    // second hue is this app's, not the platform's.

    domainTheme() {
        return ({ codeBg: Themes.sanFrancisco(this.root.isDark).bg,
            accentSecondary: this.root.isDark ? 0x37E0C8 : 0x12A594 })
        },

    // scrolling reader; the column fills the window between fixed 48px gutters, so
    // code grows with the window while prose stays capped at its reading measure.
    // `foot` sits just below the active view for a bottom margin matching `topM`.

    content: View [ x = 0, y = { this.root.barH }, width = { this.root.hostWidth }, height = { this.root.hostHeight - this.root.barH },
        visible = { this.root.mode != "edit" },
        scrolls = y, selectable = true, fill = { this.root.theme.surface },

        // the filename as a page title — the directory muted, the file bold — with
        // a rule under it; the body starts below (headH)

        head: View [ y = { this.root.topM }, width = { this.root.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            title: View [ layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
                d: Text [ fontSize = { 21 * this.root.fontScale }, wrap = false, textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted }, text = { this.root.dirName() } ],
                n: Text [ fontSize = { 21 * this.root.fontScale }, fontWeight = bold, wrap = false, textColor = { this.root.theme.text }, text = { this.root.baseName() } ],

                // the size of the thing, quietly: the compiler's own count

                gapm: View [ width = 10, height = 1 ],
                m: Text [ y = { 8 * this.root.fontScale }, fontSize = { 13 * this.root.fontScale }, wrap = false,
                    textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted }, text = { this.root.metaLabel() } ]
                ],

            // a blue→teal thread of the brand accent, the origin of the code spine

            rule: View [ y = { 34 * this.root.fontScale }, width = { parent.width }, height = 2, cornerRadius = 1,
                opacity = { this.root.isDark ? 0.72 : 1 },
                fill = { gradient("90deg", this.root.theme.accent, this.root.theme.accentSecondary) } ]
            ],

        // highlighted view: prose + colored code segments

        col: View [ visible = { this.root.mode == "reader" }, y = { this.root.topM + this.root.headH }, width = { this.root.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            datapath = { this.root.doc.value },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = y, spacing = 12 ],
            Block [ datapath = :segments[], kind = :kind, md = :md, html = :html, nested = { this.$data(["nested"]) == true }, joinBelow = { this.$data(["joinBelow"]) == true } ]
            ],

        // plain view: the verbatim source as one monospace flow (same size/theme)

        plain: View [ visible = { this.root.mode == "source" }, y = { this.root.topM + this.root.headH }, width = { this.root.hostWidth - 96 },
            x = { Math.max(24, (parent.width - this.width) / 2) },
            fill = { this.root.theme.codeBg }, cornerRadius = 8, clip = true,
            height = { this.body.height + 32 },
            spine: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 2, height = { parent.height }, fill = { this.root.theme.accentSecondary } ],

            // verbatim source at the house code rendition — the same face and size
            // as the reader's highlighted code, so the two views read identically.

            body: View [ x = 20, y = 16, width = { parent.width - 40 }, scrolls = x, height = { this.contentHeight },
                HTMLText [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { parent.width }, html = { this.root.plainHtml() },
                    scale = { this.root.fontScale }, bodyColor = { this.root.codeFg() }, selectable = true ]
                ]
            ],

        // bottom margin: a spacer just past the active view's bottom edge

        foot: View [ width = 8, height = 48,
            y = { this.root.topM + this.root.headH + (this.root.mode == "reader" ? parent.col.height : parent.plain.height) } ]
        ],

    // Live-edit workbench — a fixed stack filling the window below the bar: the
    // source in an editor on top, the running program below, compile errors
    // sandwiched between. The pieces are the host's generic live loop: the island
    // is named "run:__raw__" (its seed IS the viewed file), the editor publishes
    // every keystroke on liveCard/liveSource, and app.liveReport carries the last
    // recompile's rendered report ("" = clean; the island keeps the last good
    // render while it shows). A file with no App declaration reports instead of
    // running — honest, if unglamorous.

    // An INCLUDE on the Edit tab: it declares components and no App, so there
    // is nothing to run — one centred line points at the one program this page
    // actually knows, the one it opened on. (Which programs include a file is
    // unknowable in general — any program may — so the message claims nothing
    // about inclusion.)

    noRun: View [ visible = { this.root.mode == "edit" && this.root.isInclude }, x = 0, y = { this.root.barH },
        width = { this.root.hostWidth }, height = { this.root.hostHeight - this.root.barH }, fill = { this.root.theme.surface },

        // two centred lines with a blank line between; the second names the
        // page's own program when it has one, and claims nothing otherwise

        l1: Text [ x = center, y = { parent.height / 2 - 44 * this.root.fontScale }, wrap = false,
            fontSize = { 15 * this.root.fontScale }, textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted },
            text = "This file declares components — there is no App to run." ],

        row: View [ visible = { this.root.seededRunnable }, x = center, y = { parent.l1.y + 44 * this.root.fontScale },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
            Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * this.root.fontScale }, textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted }, text = "Edit " ],
            name: Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * this.root.fontScale }, fontWeight = semibold,
                textColor = { this.root.isDark ? 0x58A6FF : 0x0969DA },

                // a location WRITE, not a `link` attr: "edit" is the viewer's own
                // location grammar, not a `shows` destination — the registry
                // (rightly) refuses the literal form, and the write is the same
                // edge the tabs emit

                text = { this.root.seededPath().split("/").pop() || "" },
                onClick() { this.root.location = "edit" }
                ],
            Text [ wrap = false, fontSize = { 15 * this.root.fontScale }, textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted }, text = ", the program this page opened on." ]
            ],

        alt: Text [ visible = { !this.root.seededRunnable }, x = center, y = { parent.l1.y + 44 * this.root.fontScale }, wrap = false,
            fontSize = { 15 * this.root.fontScale }, textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted },
            text = "Open a program that includes it to edit live." ]
        ],

    live: View [ visible = { this.root.mode == "edit" && !this.root.isInclude }, x = 0, y = { this.root.barH },
        width = { this.root.hostWidth }, height = { this.root.hostHeight - this.root.barH },
        fill = { this.root.theme.surface },

        // the divider y: 0 = not dragged yet (a 42% default); the grip writes it

        split: number = 0,
        editorH: number = { this.split > 0 ? this.split : Math.floor(this.height * 0.42) },
        edited: boolean = false,    // an edit exists (arms Revert; onInput sets it)

        editor: TextInput [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.editorH },
            multiline = true, spellcheck = false, wrap = false, padding = 14,

            // the A stepper drives every pane, this one included — it read as a
            // dead control here, since the tab it is showing ignored it

            fontFamily = [Mono, "monospace"], fontSize = { 12 * this.root.fontScale },
            textColor = { this.root.codeFg() },
            fill = { this.root.theme.codeBg },
            initial = { this.root.demoSources["__raw__"] || this.root.rawSrc.value || "" },
            onInput() { parent.edited = true; this.root.liveCard = "__raw__"; this.root.liveSource = this.text }
            ],

        // Revert — restores the file's pristine text and recompiles it; armed
        // only once an edit exists, quiet (and inert) until then

        revert: View [ y = 10, height = 24, cornerRadius = 6,
            x = { parent.width - this.width - 14 },
            width = { this.lbl.width + 18 },
            opacity = { parent.edited ? 1 : 0.35 },
            stroke = { stroke(1, this.root.theme.line) },
            fill = { this.hovered && parent.edited ? this.root.theme.controlHover : this.root.theme.control },
            onClick() {
                if (!parent.edited) return
                const raw = this.root.demoSources["__raw__"] || this.root.rawSrc.value || ""
                parent.editor.text = raw
                parent.edited = false
                this.root.liveCard = "__raw__"; this.root.liveSource = raw
                },
            lbl: Text [ fontSize = 11, fontWeight = semibold, wrap = false,
                x = { (parent.width - this.width) / 2 }, y = { (parent.height - this.height) / 2 },
                textColor = { this.root.theme.textMuted }, text = "Revert" ]
            ],

        // the divider: the press captures the pointer to this view (the router's
        // capture model — the calendar's drag uses the same), so its move/up fire
        // for the whole drag wherever the pointer goes. The move reads the
        // POINTER's app-space y (its own event coords are grip-local and the
        // grip is what's moving); the shield above merely blocks the browser's
        // native text selection in the editor beneath.

        grip: View [ x = 0, y = { parent.editorH }, width = { parent.width }, height = 6,
            dragging: boolean = false,
            fill = { this.dragging || this.hovered ? this.root.theme.accentSecondary : this.root.theme.line },
            drag(y: number) { parent.split = Math.max(120, Math.min(parent.height - 160, y)) },
            onPointerDown()  { this.dragging = true },
            onPointerMove()  { if (this.dragging) this.drag(this.root.pointerY - this.root.barH) },
            onPointerUp()    { this.dragging = false }
            ],

        // the error sandwich: the last recompile's report IN FULL, only while one
        // stands — the wrapped multi-line text is the docs/homepage treatment (a
        // single unwrapped line showed only the report's "1 error" summary)

        report: View [ visible = { this.root.liveReport != "" }, x = 0, y = { parent.editorH + 6 },
            width = { parent.width }, clip = true,
            height = { Math.min(200, this.msg.height + 20) },
            fill = { this.root.isDark ? 0x2A1517 : 0xFDECEC },
            bar: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = 3, height = { parent.height }, fill = { this.root.isDark ? 0xE0525E : 0xC93B47 } ],
            msg: Text [ x = 14, y = 10, width = { parent.width - 28 }, wrap = true,
                fontFamily = [Mono, "monospace"], fontSize = 11,
                textColor = { this.root.isDark ? 0xFF8B8B : 0xB42318 }, text = { this.root.liveReport } ]
            ],

        // the running program — an embedded child app in a host island, swapped
        // to each clean recompile (renderChild); a floor-declaring app pans here

        run: AppIsland [ x = 0, y = { parent.editorH + 6 + (this.root.liveReport != "" ? parent.report.height : 0) },
            width = { parent.width },
            height = { parent.height - this.y },
            program = { this.root.mode == "edit" ? "__raw__" : "" } ],

        // the drag shield — last child, so it sits over everything while a
        // divider drag is on. The ROUTER already captures the drag to the grip;
        // this view's whole job is to be the browser's native hit target, so the
        // editor's textarea underneath cannot rubber-band a text selection.

        shield: View [ visible = { parent.grip.dragging }, x = 0, y = 0,
            width = { parent.width }, height = { parent.height } ]
        ],

    // top bar: the brand (left) · Reader / Source / Edit (centre) · type-size
    // stepper + theme (right). The brand is the house rendition — gradient
    // "Declare", solid app name — sized and placed as in Calendar and Docs.

    bar: View [ x = 0, y = 0, width = { this.root.hostWidth }, height = { this.root.barH }, fill = { this.root.theme.bg },

        hair: View [ x = 0, y = { this.root.barH - 1 }, width = { parent.width }, height = 1, fill = { this.root.theme.line } ],

        brand: View [ x = 20, y = { (this.root.barH - 22) / 2 }, height = 22,
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 5 ],

            // "Declare" is the way home — navigate() resolves against the distro
            // root, so this works on either host at any mount point

            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * this.fontSize }, wrap = false,
                textFill = { gradient("90deg", this.root.theme.accent, this.root.theme.accentSecondary) }, text = "Declare",
                onClick() { this.root.navigate("apps/homepage/homepage.declare") }
                ],
            Text [ fontSize = 18, fontWeight = semibold, letterSpacing = { -0.02 * this.fontSize }, wrap = false,
                textColor = { this.root.theme.text }, text = "Viewer" ]
            ],

        // Reader / Source / Edit. The tab writes `app.location`, and `app.mode`
        // derives back from it — so the switch stays a single source of truth
        // that back/forward walk for free, which is what the location comment
        // above already wanted. `Segmented` keeps that seam intact: `value` reads
        // the derived mode, `input` writes the location.

        modeSwitch: Segmented [ y = { (this.root.barH - 30) / 2 }, height = 30, width = 244,
            x = { Math.max(200, (this.root.hostWidth - 244) / 2) },
            replace = true,        // a tab switch never buries Back — the walk is between FILES
            value = { this.root.mode },

            // KEEP the viewed file across tabs: a bare `location = v` here
            // silently dropped the followed include (the choice's own location
            // carries the suffix, but this write ran after it and won the
            // settle). The keyboard path (Enter on a segment) arrives only
            // here, so this must build the full location itself — and replace,
            // like the click path, so no tab switch ever buries Back.

            input(v: object) { this.root.follow("#" + ("" + v) + (this.root.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + this.root.fileRel), true) },

            // each tab states its location, which is what makes the switch a LINK
            // the crawler can follow — without it this app emits one document
            // (the default) and Source and Edit are unreachable to extraction

            // …and keeps the viewed FILE: switching tabs on a followed include
            // stays on that include

            choices = { [ ({ id: "reader", label: "Reader", location: "reader" + (this.root.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + this.root.fileRel) }),
                          ({ id: "source", label: "Source", location: "source" + (this.root.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + this.root.fileRel) }),
                          ({ id: "edit",   label: "Edit",   location: "edit" + (this.root.fileRel == "" ? "" : "/" + this.root.fileRel) }) ] }
            ],

        size: View [ y = { (this.root.barH - 30) / 2 }, x = { parent.themeSwitch.x - this.width - 8 }, height = 30,
            width = { this.contentWidth },
            cornerRadius = 8, fill = { this.root.theme.surface }, stroke = { stroke(1, this.root.theme.line) },
            layout: SimpleLayout [ axis = x, spacing = 0 ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 11, delta = -0.1 ],
            d1: View [ width = 1, height = 18, y = 6, fill = { this.root.theme.line } ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 15, delta = 0 ],
            d2: View [ width = 1, height = 18, y = 6, fill = { this.root.theme.line } ],
            SizeBtn [ glyph = 19, delta = 0.1 ]
            ],

        themeSwitch: Segmented [ y = { (this.root.barH - 30) / 2 }, x = { this.root.hostWidth - 94 - 16 },
            height = 30, width = 94, iconSize = 15,
            value = { this.root.themeMode },
            input(v: object) { this.root.themeMode = "" + v },
            choices = { [ ({ id: "light", icon: "SunIcon" }),
                          ({ id: "auto",  icon: "AutoIcon" }),
                          ({ id: "dark",  icon: "MoonIcon" }) ] }
            ]
        ]
    ,
    // the traveling focus indicator — provided with the component library

    FocusRing [ ],
